# `js/no-parameters-only-used-in-recursion`

**No parameter that is only passed to the function's own recursive call**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-js` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-js` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX |
| **Turned on by** | no preset — name it in `[rules]` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | none — severity only |
| **Fix** | `suggest` — `codelaw fix --unsafe` applies it; review the diff, it can change behaviour (removing a parameter changes the signature, which callers see; the suggestion only marks it unused with a leading underscore) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.5.1 |
| **Ported from** | `biome/suspicious/noParametersOnlyUsedInRecursion`, `clippy/only_used_in_recursion` |

## What it checks

A parameter of a named function (or of a method called as `this.name(…)`) whose every read is the argument, at its own position, of a recursive call — alone or as the left side of `||`/`??` — is reported. A parameter read anywhere else (returned, compared, passed to another function) is used. The suggestion prefixes the parameter and those arguments with `_`. Behaviour of Biome's `noParametersOnlyUsedInRecursion`.

**Why:** The value goes around the recursion and nothing ever looks at it, so the parameter does no work and the callers pay to compute it.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-js
pip install codelaw-rules-js
```

**No preset turns it on.** Load its pack through any preset (`codelaw:js/recommended` here), then name the rule in `[rules]`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:js/recommended"]

[rules]
"js/no-parameters-only-used-in-recursion" = "error"
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"js/no-parameters-only-used-in-recursion" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — the `tests` scope `codelaw:js/recommended` ships (`**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`); naming it extends it, so its files stay:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/no-parameters-only-used-in-recursion" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"js/no-parameters-only-used-in-recursion" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"js/no-parameters-only-used-in-recursion" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"js/no-parameters-only-used-in-recursion" = { severity = "warn" }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "js/no-parameters-only-used-in-recursion": {"severity": "warn"}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JavaScript:** `// codelaw-ignore js/no-parameters-only-used-in-recursion: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore js/no-parameters-only-used-in-recursion expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule js/no-parameters-only-used-in-recursion --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain js/no-parameters-only-used-in-recursion       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule js/no-parameters-only-used-in-recursion  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>                           # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## Examples

### JavaScript

#### Don't

```js
function sum(n, acc) {
  if (n === 0) return 0;
  return n + sum(n - 1, acc);
}
```

#### Do

```js
function sum(n, _acc) {
  if (n === 0) return 0;
  return n + sum(n - 1, _acc);
}
```

#### Fixed

```js
function sum(n, _acc) {
  if (n === 0) return 0;
  return n + sum(n - 1, _acc);
}
```
